blocWeather.blocWeatherInfo:
Rock moisture indicates how wet the rock surface is likely to be, based on recent precipitation, humidity, wind, solar radiation, and the modelled rock surface temperature.
0% = likely dry · 100% = fully saturated. The shaded area shows the range between the best case (sun-exposed) and the worst case (shaded, north-facing).

scale.scaleForm.gradeBracketsDescription: The intervals for stacked bar charts are defined here. The intervals view is built as follows. Suppose the intervals are [5, 10, 15, 16]. Then the first section will include all grades with a value up to 5, the next one those between 6 and 10, then 11 to 15 and finally everything from 16 onwards. The last two values must be consecutive and the intervals must be sorted. Projects are always grouped separately. Each interval has its own color.

gallery.galleryForm.addGalleryImageDescr:
Upload an image and add tags to make it appear in the corresponding galleries.

Concrete boulders require a tag with the name of the line and the climber (if applicable).Other photos (e.g. panoramic) mainly require a tag for the area in which they were taken.

projectClimbedForm.projectClimbedInfoMes: You climbed a project? Congratulations! It would be great if you could send us some information so that we can include the new line in the topo. First and foremost are the line name and the proposed difficulty rating. If you have a video, feel free to send it to us. If you want to be mentioned in the Topo for the first ascent, send us your name and the date of the ascent. We will be in touch!

releaseNotes.notes.frenchLanguage: French can now be selected as a language. If you are logged in, you can change your language in the account settings.
releaseNotes.notes.lineFilters: In list view, you can now filter lines by any property—such as starting position or hold type—with one click on the filter button. Selected filters are saved locally and are available immediately in all lists.
releaseNotes.notes.newOrderOptions: In list view, you can now sort lines by record date and by their position on the topo (block or photo). Crags, sectors, and areas can be sorted by number of lines and by total ascent count.

releaseNotes.notes.darkMode: As you can see, there was a bigger redesign! The somewhat old-school large background images were removed; instead there are header images matching the crag, sector, and line. You can also enable dark mode in your account settings. Feedback welcome at: https://github.com/LocalCrag/LocalCragApp
